source_name: EIB Group Supplier Portal
why_relevant: Registration and opportunity channel for EIB/EIF corporate and technical-assistance procurement — the route by which advisory/IT contracts with Hungarian financial-sector scope are competed outside Hungary.

source_name: EU Funding & Tenders Portal — EIB/EIF call for tender notices
why_relevant: EIB corporate tenders carry EIB/YYYY/OP/nnnn references and are published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal; this is a machine-searchable, non-Hungarian channel for contracts whose delivery scope can include Hungary.

source_name: EIB Project Procurement guidance + Guide to Procurement (PDF)
why_relevant: Defines that EIB-financed promoters must publish notices in the OJEU/TED and, where applicable, on the EIB website — i.e. tells the collector exactly which downstream feeds carry EIB-driven Hungarian contracts.

source_name: EIF Procurement — how it works
why_relevant: The EIF procures separately from the EIB and mandates guarantee/equity instruments delivered through Hungarian financial intermediaries; its procurement of advisory and platform services is a cross-border channel invisible to Hungarian portals.

source_name: Erste Group Procurement (Erste Group Bank AG subsidiary page, DE/EN)
why_relevant: Erste Group Procurement (incl. Procurement Services Ges.m.b.H. / s ProServ) is the group-level buying entity that runs e-auctions and the group e-procurement platform covering CEE subsidiaries including Erste Bank Hungary. Supplier documents, code of conduct and general terms of purchase define how a vendor can even be considered for Hungarian bank spend.

source_name: Erste Bank Hungary — Fenntartható és etikus beszállítói lánc (sustainable/ethical supplier chain)
why_relevant: Hungarian-language confirmation that a group procurement unit is the EXCLUSIVE procurement service provider for Erste Bank Hungary and its subsidiaries, that tenders run on the Erste Group Procurement online platform, and it discloses supplier-base metrics (c. 2,230 Hungarian suppliers, 105 major partners). Directly evidences the cell hypothesis that Hungarian bank spend is decided on a group platform.

source_name: RBI Group Supplier Code of Conduct — Hungarian version (PDF)
why_relevant: Group-issued, Hungarian-language supplier rulebook applying to all RBI suppliers delivering goods, services or licences — the compliance gate any vendor to Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. must pass. Its existence in Hungarian shows group-level terms being pushed down to the Hungarian subsidiary.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International — Group Procurement, Outsourcing & Real Estate Management (function profile)
why_relevant: RBI runs a centralised Group Procurement function (Head: Edzard Janssen) covering 24 CEE markets, explicitly pursuing centralised digital procurement and category management — meaning Hungarian Raiffeisen vendor decisions are largely Vienna-set. Function-level signals (strategy pillars, platform choices) predict what Hungarian subsidiaries will buy.

source_name: Procurement vendor case studies on RBI (akirolabs, CPOstrategy)
why_relevant: Vendor-published case studies and CPO interviews reveal, in the vendor's own words, which procurement/category-management platforms a CEE banking group adopted and how centralised sourcing is organised across subsidiaries — a rare window into decisions never tendered publicly.

source_name: FISAC CGIL — UniCredit Services procurement reorganisation reporting (Italian trade union)
why_relevant: Italian union sources report internal UniCredit procurement reorganisation and tooling in detail — e.g. the move of supplier tendering and qualification from legacy modules (GSD, Agorà) onto SAP Ariba, and who operates it. UniCredit Bank Hungary's vendor selection sits inside exactly this group machinery, which UniCredit itself does not disclose publicly.

source_name: UniCredit Group corporate portal (supplier/corporate gateway)
why_relevant: Entry point to UniCredit group-level corporate systems; relevant as the identified access surface for group supplier/tender interactions, though authenticated. Useful mainly to document that UniCredit's Hungarian vendor pipeline is behind a group login rather than any public notice board.

source_name: K&H Bank (kh.hu) corporate/about pages — KBC-owned Hungarian subsidiary
why_relevant: Confirms and documents K&H's ownership by KBC Group (Brussels) and its scale (c. 4,000 staff, 226 retail + 12 corporate branches), establishing that K&H procurement policy and major platform decisions are set at Belgian group level. Baseline actor-map source for the Belgian leg of this cell.

source_name: MNB recommendation 7/2020 on use of external service providers (outsourcing) + MNB institution search
why_relevant: Transposes EBA/GL/2019/02 and obliges Hungarian institutions to maintain a documented outsourcing register recording the external provider's identity, company registration number, tax number, seat, contacts AND THE PARENT COMPANY NAME, plus criticality. This is the regulatory hook that makes intra-group and cross-border sourcing arrangements documentable and, in part, discoverable via supervisory disclosures and banks' own business rules (üzletszabályzat), which must list outsourced activities and their performers.

source_name: MNB recommendation 1/2025 and 13/2025 on IT systems / banking digitalisation
why_relevant: MNB requires institutions to regulate IT governance, planning, development AND PROCUREMENT ('beszerzés'), operations and independent control. These recommendations shape what group-level platform rollouts must satisfy locally, and are the vocabulary source for Hungarian procurement/IT terms used in bank filings.

source_name: Erste Bank Hungary base prospectus / BÉT (bet.hu) issuer filings
why_relevant: Hungarian subsidiary issuer documents describe group affiliation, intra-group service arrangements and material outsourcing/dependency on the Austrian parent — a way to reveal group-level sourcing dependencies that are never announced as tenders.

source_name: Commercial IFI tender aggregators (TendersOnTime, GlobalTenders, TendersInfo, BidDetail)
why_relevant: Paid aggregators re-index EBRD/EIB notices and sometimes surface items faster or with better country tagging than the primary portals. Useful only as a cross-check/backfill layer, never as a primary or citable source.

source_name: CEE banking sector M&A / market studies and CEE Legal Matters guides
why_relevant: CEE-wide legal and M&A studies map which groups own which Hungarian banks and how regional consolidation is moving — the ownership layer that determines where a Hungarian bank's procurement authority actually sits, and which regional frameworks a Hungarian entity is likely to be pulled into.

source_name: Hungarian business/economic press on foreign bank groups' Hungary strategy (e.g. Telex gazdaság)
why_relevant: Hungarian-language reporting on whether foreign-owned groups (Erste, UniCredit, CIB/Intesa, Raiffeisen, K&H) stay or exit the market is a leading indicator of whether group-level investment and platform rollouts will be extended to or withdrawn from the Hungarian subsidiary.

source_name: MNB – Közbeszerzés (Közérdekű adatok / Gazdálkodási adatok)
why_relevant: Statutory disclosure page of the Hungarian central bank as a contracting authority (ajánlatkérő) under Kbt. 2015/CXLIII; carries the annual procurement plan (közbeszerzési terv), notices and statistical summaries for MNB's own supplier tenders, which include core banking/payments and cash-logistics IT.

source_name: MNB – Beszerzési eljárások (supplier hub)
why_relevant: MNB's supplier-facing hub: e-invoicing, e-signature of contracts, contract annexes and the procurement/public-procurement archive. Tells us how MNB contracts with vendors and where notices land; verified by fetch to list subpages.

source_name: MNB – Közbeszerzés (Archív) incl. yearly procedure lists (e.g. 2017)
why_relevant: Year-by-year archive of MNB public procurement procedures (e.g. 'Közbeszerzési eljárások 2017'), giving multi-year vendor/award history for IT, identity management, monitoring, digital signature infrastructure — a longitudinal baseline for who supplies the central bank.

source_name: MNB – Szerződéses mellékletek a beszerzési és közbeszerzési eljárásokban
why_relevant: Standard contract annexes MNB imposes on suppliers (security, IT, data protection requirements). Indirectly reveals technical/compliance barriers a payments vendor must clear to sell to the central bank.

source_name: MNB archívum – Egyéb beszerzési eljárások (below-threshold procurements)
why_relevant: Legacy archive covering non-Kbt. ('egyéb') procurements that never reach EKR/TED — the tier where smaller payments/ATM/service contracts often sit.

source_name: Magyar Államkincstár – Pénzforgalom / Hirdetmények
why_relevant: Treasury notices on account management, payment services and the Kincstári Kártya — not tender notices, but they signal service/technology changes (card scheme, cash handling, payment rails) that typically precede or follow a supplier procurement.

source_name: Magyar Államkincstár – institutional site (public-data / procurement disclosures)
why_relevant: The Treasury is a major contracting authority for payment processing, account systems and cash operations. Its 'rólunk / közérdekű adatok' tree is the entry point to its statutory közbeszerzési terv and contract disclosures; the exact procurement subpage URL was not confirmed in this pass.

source_name: Magyar Posta Zrt. – Beszerzések, pályázatok
why_relevant: Magyar Posta is a utility-regime contracting entity and a major buyer of cash logistics, postal-financial (Posta pénzügyi szolgáltatások) counter systems, terminals and IT. Its own tender page publishes open procedures and preliminary market consultations (előzetes piaci konzultáció).

source_name: Magyar Posta Zrt. – Beszerzési hírlevél (procurement newsletter)
why_relevant: Push channel announcing Posta procurement opportunities to suppliers; a subscription gives earlier notice than the web listing and enumerates upcoming categories.
